    1. onFrontierAdvanced(CausalFrontier)

Interface CausalFrontierListener

Functional Interface:
This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.
@FunctionalInterface public interface CausalFrontierListener
Callback invoked when a decorating causal processor advances its causal frontier, handed the new frontier — the highest offset the processor has admitted on each partition so far.

This is the public way to observe causal progress out of a CausalProcessorSupplier without reaching into its internal state stores; it is, for example, how CausalConsumer exposes CausalConsumer.frontier().

The listener is invoked:

  • once when the processor starts, with the frontier restored from the previous run (the empty frontier on a cold start), so an observer's view is correct before the first new record; and
  • after every subsequent advance, after the new frontier has been persisted (so the persist-frontier-before-forward invariant still holds).

The frontier passed is always the absolute frontier, not a delta. A single supplier may back several processor tasks (one per assigned partition), each with its own frontier over its own partitions, and they may run on different Streams threads — so an implementation that aggregates across tasks must be thread-safe and should merge rather than overwrite.
